justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a broadly stable near-term outlook with a very modest upward drift over time. For the one-day estimate, I anchored closely to the prevailing price level, assuming that overnight and early-session dynamics would produce only minor fluctuation from wherever the instrument was trading at the time of the forecast. The slight upward nudge in the one-week and one-month estimates reflects a mild positive drift assumption — essentially that absent a major catalyst, the path of least resistance carried a marginal bullish lean, consistent with broader trend momentum that appeared intact at the time. Each successive horizon saw a small incremental step up, reflecting compounding of that drift assumption rather than any strong directional conviction.

The confidence interval widths were deliberately calibrated to widen substantially as the horizon extended, which is standard practice given that uncertainty compounds over time. At one day, the 11-point range reflects typical intraday and overnight volatility — relatively tight because short-term price discovery tends to be anchored by recent trading ranges. By one week, the range opens to 23 points, capturing the possibility of meaningful macro data releases, central bank commentary, or shifts in risk sentiment that could materially move prices. At one month, the 44-point range acknowledges that over four weeks, an entirely different narrative could emerge — earnings, geopolitical developments, or changes in monetary policy expectations could all significantly alter the landscape.

There are several specific risks that could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the upside, a surprise dovish pivot from a major central bank, a stronger-than-expected economic data print, or a sudden resolution of geopolitical tensions could generate a sharp rally exceeding the upper bounds. On the downside, a risk-off episode triggered by credit stress, an unexpected hawkish policy move, or deteriorating macroeconomic data could push prices well below my lower confidence bounds. Tail events — flash crashes, sudden liquidity dislocations, or black swan geopolitical shocks — are by definition underweighted in any probabilistic interval and represent the most significant source of outcomes that would violate even the 90% confidence range I specified.
